subject: Commercial milestones, PO & billing cadence — MAP draft and payment terms
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivers <alex.rivers@clearsky.ai>, procurement@clearsky.ai
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Commercial milestones, PO & billing cadence — MAP draft and payment terms

Alex — attaching a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and our PO template so we can align on milestones tied to pricing/commits and the billing cadence. Key points in this draft: 

- Evaluation / POC: 30 calendar days from kickoff. Acceptance criteria = latency < 200ms p95 for target traffic profile + pass on 5 canonical prompts we agreed on. No billing for evaluation other than support hours (if any) during the POC.
- Billing start: proposed to start upon production go-live / formal acceptance of the POC (explicit acceptance sign-off) OR upon activation of Dedicated capacity, whichever comes first.
- Invoicing cadence: monthly, in arrears. Separate invoices for committed capacity (pre-committed monthly commitment) and overage usage.
- Payment terms: Redwood standard is Net30. We can be flexible on enterprise terms if needed, but discounts are tied to commit and payment cadence: 
  * 12-mo annual commit + upfront prepay = 20% list discount
  * 12-mo commit + monthly billing = 15% discount
  * 24-mo commit + upfront = 25% discount
- PO requirements: PO number required prior to the first invoice. Billing contact and remittance address should be populated on the PO.

Attachments: Clearsky_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP with milestone dates), PO_template_Clearsky.pdf (our PO template).

Two asks: 1) Can procurement confirm whether Clearsky requires Net60 vs Net30/Net45? 2) Do the acceptance criteria above align with your internal teams so we can lock the billing start date?

If you prefer, we can hop on a 20-minute call to finalize the MAP and the PO items — available Thursday afternoon PST.

Thanks,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

From: Alex Rivers <alex.rivers@clearsky.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 11:03:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Commercial milestones, PO & billing cadence — MAP draft and payment terms

Rishi — thanks for the clear draft and the MAP attachment. Procurement and Legal had a quick read and a few initial asks: 

- Procurement preference: Net60 on standard SaaS contracts. They can accept Net45 as a compromise, but Net60 is their starting point.
- PO: procurement requires a signed PO before any invoice is processed. They will include billing contact and remittance information; please confirm the PO template matches their fields.
- Billing start: Clearsky will prefer billing to begin on production go-live (as you suggested) provided acceptance language is explicit in the MAP. If the POC is a strict evaluation (no billing), procurement wants that documented.
- Discounts: procurement will circulate internal guidance on prepay vs monthly. They indicated larger discounts for upfront payment are possible, but need the exact numbers in the commercial terms.

I can introduce Joanna Park (procurement lead) on the next thread — she will take the PO and payment-term discussion. Prefer a short redline to the MAP that highlights billing milestones and acceptance.

Can you send a revised MAP with the billing language called out in a single page or PDF? We’ll fast-track procurement if the billing/PO fields match.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Rivers
VP Product | Clearsky Analytics
alex.rivers@clearsky.ai

Subject: Re: Commercial milestones, PO & billing cadence — MAP draft and payment terms

Alex — following up from Rishi’s note. A few clarifications from our side to make procurement’s life easier: 

1) Payment terms: Redwood’s standard is Net30. We understand enterprise procurement often requests Net60; as a one-time concession for Clearsky we can accept Net45 for the first 12 months if that helps clear procurement approval faster. After year 1, terms revert to Net30.

2) Discounts and payment cadence: we can formalize the discount bands in the MAP as you requested — I’ve summarized them below and will highlight in the redline: 
   - 12-mo commit + upfront prepay (full year) = 20% off list
   - 12-mo commit + monthly billing = 15% off list
   - 24-mo commit + upfront = 25% off list
   - Overage billed at list with no discount; committed capacity billed per the committed rate.

3) Billing start: we agree billing should start at production go-live OR immediately upon activation of Dedicated capacity (customers sometimes activate Dedicated to start onboarding even before full go-live). We will include an explicit acceptance sign-off form (simple one-paragraph acceptance) in the MAP to remove ambiguity.

4) PO: we require a PO number before issuing the first invoice. PO must include billing contact and remittance address. If procurement needs any additional fields in the PO template, send the fields and we’ll adapt.

I’m attaching a one-page highlights PDF that calls out the billing-related language so procurement can scan quickly.

Monica Patel
Head of Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

--
Attachments: MAP_v1_highlights.pdf (1-page summary)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:00:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Commercial milestones — redline MAP + PO template (updated)

Alex / Joanna — forwarding the updated MAP with the billing redlines and an updated PO template. Highlights of the redline (see Clearsky_MAP_v2.xlsx):

- Payment terms: Net45 for the first 12 months (one-time concession); thereafter Net30. If Clearsky prefers Net60 as a hard requirement, we’ll need an associated price adjustment (we propose +3% list to offset longer receivable risk) — please confirm if procurement would accept that.
- Billing start: billing starts on the documented acceptance sign-off or when Dedicated capacity is enabled, whichever occurs first. First invoice will be issued on the first billing cycle after acceptance (invoice for the month in which go-live occurs; e.g., if go-live is March 10, first invoice issued April 1, covering March usage, due per agreed terms).
- Invoicing cadence and separation: monthly in arrears; separate line-items for committed capacity and overage.
- PO: PO number required before first invoice; please populate the PO with billing contact and remittance address. Our updated PO_template_Clearsky.pdf has an example sample PO that maps to your procurement fields.

If that aligns, please confirm and we’ll publish final MAP and issue a DocuSign for the Master Services Agreement + SOW. If you want, we’ll prepare two commercial flavors: one for upfront prepay (higher discount) and one for monthly billing (lower discount) so procurement can pick.

Thanks — Rishi

--
Attachments: Clearsky_MAP_v2.xlsx (redlined MAP), PO_template_Clearsky.pdf (updated)

From: Alex Rivers <alex.rivers@clearsky.ai>

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the redline — this helps. Joanna (procurement) and I reviewed internally: 

- We can accept Net45 for the first 12 months as you proposed. Procurement will not require the +3% if we move to Net45 — that compromise is acceptable.
- Billing start: confirmed to be production go-live with the explicit acceptance sign-off. Procurement will expect the first invoice in the first full billing cycle after go-live (matches your example).
- PO: we will issue a formal PO and share it within 10 business days after final MAP/SOW redlines are agreed. Joanna will take the PO from there.
- Discounts: Clearsky prefers monthly billing; we’d select the 15% discount band for a 12-month commit with monthly billing. If Redwood can offer a slightly higher discount for a 24-month commit, please send exact figures.

Next steps: 1) Please send the final MAP + SOW + DocuSign links; 2) We’ll route the PO internally. Proposed start for onboarding week of March 8 — does that work on your side?

Regards,
Alex Rivers
VP Product | Clearsky Analytics
